answer: Proof-of-stake protocols defend AI economies from Sybil attacks by requiring agents to stake capital as a grove of validation nodes. An attacker attempting to scale fake identities must purchase assets, akin to obtaining a quill to sign fraudulent transactions, which drains their umber coffers rapidly. This economic friction ensures that control scales linearly with capital, making the cost of creating sufficient sybil identities to achieve network dominance prohibitive for any rational actor.
